SA Text Assembly at a Glance

This page gives the line forms and instruction shapes of .sa text assembly; all examples are taken from real files in the repository under demos/rosetta/. After reading it you will be able to read an existing .sa, and to write a minimal program following the examples.

Top-Level Structure

Each top-level element occupies one line or one block; the main forms are (see design document §3.1, the source text protocol):

FormExample
Import / constant@import "sa_std/io/print.sai", @const HELLO_MSG = utf8:"hello\n"
Offset constant#def Point_x = +0, #loc "main.rs":42:7 (upstream location pseudo-instruction)
Function definition@main() -> i32:; add ! for fallible: @compute() -> i32!:
Borrow / ownership parameters@fill_zero(&arr: ptr) -> void:, @process_msg(^msg: ptr) -> i32:
External declaration / export@extern fd_open(*path: ptr) -> i32, @export add_pair(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32:
Airlock function@ffi_wrapper mmap_view(fd: i32, len: i32) -> &ptr:
Label / macro / native escapeL_ENTRY:, [MACRO]…[END_MACRO], [REP 8] + EXPAND 名字 …, $ … $

A Complete Minimal Program

From demos/rosetta/01_hello_world/main.sa:

@import "sa_std/io/print.sai"

@const HELLO_MSG = utf8:"hello, saasm\n"

@main() -> i32:
L_ENTRY:
    call @sa_print_bytes(&HELLO_MSG, 13)
    return 0

Typical Shapes for Memory and Control Flow

From demos/rosetta/02_mutability/main.sa, showing alloc/borrow/store and branching:

    x = alloc 8
    store x+0, 10 as i64

    r1 = &x
    before = load r1+0 as i64
    !r1

    r2 = &x
    store r2+0, 20 as i64
    !r2

    ok_before = eq before, 10
    ok_after = eq after, 20
    ok = and ok_before, ok_after
    br ok -> L_OK, L_ERR

L_OK:
    !ok
    call @sa_print_bytes(&RESULT_OK, 3)
    return 0
NoteSA has no if/else/while keywords — forms such as {}, if, while, and a.b.c appearing in source code directly trigger ForbiddenSyntax. All branches are expressed with br + labels.

Loops: Hand-Written goto State Machines

From demos/rosetta/04_loop/main.sa:

@fill_zero(&arr: ptr) -> void:
L_ENTRY:
    i_slot = stack_alloc 8
    store i_slot+0, 0 as u64
    jmp L_COND

L_COND:
    i = load i_slot+0 as u64
    more = ult i, 4
    br more -> L_BODY, L_END

L_BODY:
    slot = ptr_add arr, i
    store slot+0, 0 as u8
    next = add i, 1
    store i_slot+0, next as u64
    !slot
    !next
    !i
    !more
    jmp L_COND

L_END:
    !i
    !more
    !arr
    return

Vtables and Indirect Calls

From demos/rosetta/07_trait_vtable/main.sa:

@const BUTTON_VT = vtable { draw = @button_draw }

@render(&item: ptr) -> i32:
L_ENTRY:
    data_ptr = load item+DynDraw_DATA as ptr
    vtable_ptr = load item+DynDraw_VTABLE as ptr
    draw_fn = load vtable_ptr+VTable_draw as ptr
    result = call_indirect draw_fn(&data_ptr)
    !draw_fn
    !vtable_ptr
    !data_ptr
    !item
    return result

Error Propagation and Atomic Operations

? early return (demos/rosetta/19_result_question/main.sa):

@compute() -> i32!:
L_ENTRY:
    tripled_res = call @triple_ok(7)
    value = ? tripled_res
    return value

Atomic RMW / load (demos/rosetta/109_atomic_fetch_add/main.sa):

    old = atomic_rmw_add node+Atomic_value, 3 as i32 seq_cst
    new = atomic_load node+Atomic_value as i32 seq_cst

Only five orderings are allowed: relaxed / acquire / release / acq_rel / seq_cst; a cmpxchg whose failure ordering is stronger than its success ordering reports InvalidAtomicOrdering at the flattener stage.

Quick Reference of Common Instructions (all from real .sa files or the official EBNF)

CategoryMnemonic / formDescription
Memoryalloc N, stack_alloc N, load r+off as T, store r+off, v as T, ptr_add base, iHeap allocation / stack slot / read-write / pointer advance
Arithmetic and comparisonadd sub mul sdiv udiv srem urem neg and or xor shl lshr ashr not eq ne slt sle sgt sge ult ule ugt uge fadd fsub fmul fdiv fcmp_* and conversions such as trunc zext sext fptosi sitofp bitcastUniformly written as r = op a, b
Control flowjmp L, br c -> L1, L2, call @f(...), call_indirect fn(...), return [v]A basic block must end with a terminator instruction, otherwise FallthroughForbidden
Error propagationv = ? res, panic(code)Only usable in -> T! functions
Atomicsatomic_load, atomic_store, cmpxchg, fence, atomic_rmw_{add,sub,and,or,xor,xchg,smin,smax,umin,umax}Conflicting RMW orderings on the same address trigger AtomicOrderingMismatch
Ownership!r, parameter prefixes & ^ *Release / borrow / move / raw pointer
Airlock-onlyv = *raw (rawcast), v = assume_safe r, v = assume_borrow r[, mut]Only usable inside @ffi_wrapper
Reserved in the EBNFtake, release, move, borrowAppear in the inst rule of the official EBNF; not used directly in the demo corpus

Types

Type annotations are limited to scalars and the pointer family: i8…i64, u8…u64, f32/f64, ptr, v128 (the most common in the demo corpus are i32, i64, u8, u32, ptr); using any other annotation yields UnsupportedType. Constant literals carry a type prefix, such as utf8:"text\n", vtable { draw = @button_draw }.
